title: Got $5,000? 2 Growth Stocks Building the Software Backbone of the AI Revolution
author: Leo Sun
description: The article highlights Amazon and Palantir as two AI software companies positioned to benefit from the AI market's rapid expansion. Amazon's AWS provides cloud infrastructure and AI services like Bedrock and SageMaker, with additional upside from its Anthropic stake. Palantir offers data aggregation platforms (Gotham and Foundry) that enable AI application development. Both companies are expected to deliver strong revenue and earnings growth through 2028, though Palantir trades at a premium valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: AWS is positioned as a linchpin of the AI market with strong growth prospects. The company benefits from Anthropic stake, expected 15% revenue CAGR and 24% EPS CAGR through 2028, and reasonable valuation at 25x forward earnings.

Palantir's data aggregation and AI integration capabilities position it as a key player in the AI revolution. Expected 58% revenue CAGR and 70% EPS CAGR through 2028 demonstrate strong growth, though premium valuation at 87x forward earnings is noted as a consideration.
Mentioned as a popular AI chipmaker focus, but the article positions software companies as underappreciated alternatives rather than endorsing or criticizing Nvidia.

title: Bloom Energy vs. Plug Power: Which Fuel Cell Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: Bloom Energy and Plug Power represent different approaches to the hydrogen and fuel cell market. Bloom Energy focuses on solid-oxide fuel cells for data centers with strong near-term profitability prospects, while Plug Power is building a comprehensive green hydrogen ecosystem with significant long-term potential. Despite Bloom's superior current financials and expected profitability in 2026, the article recommends Plug Power as the better long-term buy due to its dramatically lower P/S ratio and positioning in the growing renewable hydrogen market.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth (37% YoY), expected to reach $4.1B in FY2026 with 85% growth, projected swing to $658M net income, positive free cash flow of $57.2M, and benefiting from AI datacenter boom. However, carries high debt-to-equity ratio of 3.9x and currently unprofitable.

Recommended as the better long-term buy despite current losses due to dramatically lower P/S ratio (3.7x vs 25.1x), strong positioning in renewable hydrogen market with EU mandates, major customers (Amazon, Walmart) entering replacement cycles, and expected net loss narrowing to $580M in FY2026. However, faces significant cash burn ($662M negative FCF) and customer concentration risk.

title: Uber Technologies vs. DoorDash: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares Uber Technologies and DoorDash as investment options for 2026. Uber operates across mobility, delivery, and freight globally with $52B in revenue, a 19.3% net margin, and a P/E of 15.57x. DoorDash focuses on North American food and grocery delivery with $13.7B in revenue, a 6.8% net margin, and a P/E of 101.78x. The author recommends Uber due to its diversified business model, stronger profitability, and more attractive valuation, while acknowledging DoorDash as a credible long-term bet in the delivery space.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong financial performance with $52B revenue (18.3% YoY growth), 19.3% net margin, substantial free cash flow of $9.8B, attractive P/E of 15.57x, diversified business model across mobility/delivery/freight, and strategic partnerships with autonomous vehicle leaders position it as the recommended buy.

Solid growth with $13.7B revenue (27.9% YoY growth) and record membership sign-ups, but faces challenges including high P/E of 101.78x, lower net margin of 6.8%, heavy reliance on consumer incentives, and single-category focus. Acknowledged as credible but less diversified than Uber.
Mentioned as a competitor to Uber in the ridesharing space, representing competitive pressure but not analyzed in detail as a standalone investment option.
Mentioned as a competitor to DoorDash in the delivery space, representing competitive pressure but not analyzed as a primary investment focus.

title: 3 Reasons to Hold Alibaba Stock Despite Its High Premium P/S
author: Na
description: Alibaba trades at a premium valuation but offers fundamental support for existing shareholders to hold. The company's cloud and AI businesses are accelerating with AI revenues exceeding one-third of cloud sales, core e-commerce remains resilient to fund AI ambitions, and management has outlined a disciplined multi-year AI infrastructure payback plan. While near-term margin pressure from capex and quick commerce losses persists, consensus earnings growth of 76.61% for fiscal 2027 supports patience through the current investment cycle.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Accelerating cloud and AI monetization with triple-digit AI revenue growth for 12 consecutive quarters, resilient core commerce generating cash to self-fund transformation, and disciplined capital allocation framework with defined payback horizon. Consensus fiscal 2027 earnings expected to grow 76.61% YoY, supporting long-term holding thesis despite near-term headwinds.

title: CrowdStrike vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Pamela Kock
description: The article compares CrowdStrike and Palantir Technologies as investment options for 2026. CrowdStrike offers a leading cybersecurity platform with 22% revenue growth but remains unprofitable and faces reputational damage from a 2024 outage. Palantir demonstrates stronger financial performance with 56% revenue growth, profitability, and no debt, but carries higher valuation and customer concentration risks. The author recommends CrowdStrike for its better balance between growth and valuation, despite ongoing challenges.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong market position and resilient stock recovery post-outage, but offset by ongoing unprofitability (-3.4% net margin), reputational damage from July 2024 incident, and slower growth (21.7% YoY). Recommended by author as better value despite challenges.

Exceptional financial performance with 56.2% revenue growth, strong profitability (36.3% net margin), zero debt, high liquidity, and expanding commercial customer base. However, positive sentiment is tempered by high valuation multiples and customer concentration risk.
